Detection gaps allowed initial access to go unnoticed.

arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was initiated via a malicious email received by a finance user (CORP\jsmith) on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.20). The attack began with a phishing email containing a malicious link that led to the download of a Cobalt Strike beacon. Execution was achieved through an encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook, which then loaded an unsigned DLL via rundll32 from the Temp directory. The malware established a C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443 and performed host file modification. Lateral movement was detected via SMB to a file server (10.0.5.50). The threat actor attempted Kerberos TGT requests and had broad network access, indicating potential for privilege escalation and data exfiltration. Containment actions included revocation of four critical service/admin accounts (svc-backup, svc-sql-prod, admin-deploy, svc-monitoring) and forced password expiration across all 200 production servers via Ansible. No sandbox detection occurred due to evasion techniques.
